item.title: The Worst Thing That Happened to Software Development
item.description:
Unpopular opinion: LLMs are the worst thing that has happened to software development, and we will all pay the price.

Not about vibe-coders

I’m not talking about “vibe-coders”. I don’t think that phenomenon deserves serious discussion.

I’m talking about people who use AI as a coding assistant, convinced they’re still in control of their architecture and design decisions. In reality, the LLM is making those decisions for you, while keeping you under the illusion of control.

item.title: On Apple Intelligence, LLM limitations and the next AI winter
item.description: Apple Intelligence is a project that has been in the works for a while now, and it has been rumored to be a major feature in iOS 18 and the new iPhone 16. However, the project has faced several delays, and it seems that Apple is struggling to get it right. In this post, I will share my thoughts on the reasons behind these delays and what they mean for the future of Apple Intelligence and AI.

item.title: Torchtitan: A PyTorch Library for Parallelism Techniques Explained
item.description: Torchtitan is an excellent project to learn how to implement distributed training techniques for training massive language models on hundreds of GPUs. I’ve been using it for a few months, and now that the paper is out, I thought it’d be a good idea to share a few posts about how to use it, what works and what doesn’t, and what I learned while implementing these ideas in my own project.
